title: Full Recovery
concept: A six-step way to rebuild after a fight you keep having, or something that actually dented trust — a real new agreement and a set time to prove it, not just a nicer evening.
whenToUse: Use for a repeated fight, or a clear before/after dent in trust, when a normal Weekly Reset can't hold the topic. Don't use it mid-fight, as a stand-in for a smaller repair, or unless you've both agreed to sit down for it.
steps: Warm up first — soften the mood before anything else. Don't skip this.
Say what happened — both sides, no interrupting.
Acknowledge the impact — before either of you explains.
Explain, if asked — only after the impact has actually landed.
Ask for one change — name it, and agree by when.
Say it out loud — “We made it through this. We're still here.”

phrases.text: I want a Full Recovery conversation — can we schedule it for when we're both calm?
The agreement I'm asking for is ___, visible by ___.
We made it through this. We're still here.

working: Scheduled Sunday 4pm. Warmed up first. Both said what happened. Impact acknowledged. One proof item for 14 days. Said out loud they made it through. Checked in weekly on the proof.
notWorking: Bringing this up at midnight, mid-fight, both too wound up, no warm-up first. It just becomes one more injury. How and when you have this conversation matters as much as what's said.
activity: Set aside 60–90 calm minutes. Bring one issue only. Write down the agreement and the check-in date before you leave the room.
warn: Not during active conflict. Calm, agreed, scheduled — never sprung on someone.
